items.title: 3.1 Cells: the basic unit of life

source_refs.note: Chapter opening and topic 3.1, printed pages 48-49: cells as the basic unit of life and the seven properties of life.

blocks.text: Cells are the basic unit of life, making up every living organism. In unicellular organisms like amoebas and bacteria, a single cell carries out all the functions necessary for life. Multicellular organisms, such as plants and animals, are composed of numerous specialised cells that work together to sustain life.

blocks.title: What this chapter covers
blocks.text: Building on Grade IX, this chapter studies the cell theory, the structures of animal and plant cells, cell signalling, the potential of stem cells, and the membrane transport mechanisms that keep a cell working.

You know that all living organisms show the seven basic properties of life: movement, respiration, homeostasis, growth, reproduction, excretion and nutrition. These properties actually define living organisms, and cells perform all the fundamental activities that characterise them.
The seven properties of life, seen in a cell

items: Movement: cells can move. Sperm cells move with their flagella; white blood cells travel through the bloodstream to fight infections; inside cells, organelles move to carry out vital functions.
Nutrition: cells obtain nutrients from their environment to produce energy, build cellular structures and drive biochemical reactions.
Respiration: cells generate energy through respiration. This process breaks glucose to release ATP, the energy currency that powers cellular activities.
Excretion: cells remove waste products through diffusion and active transport, preventing toxic build-up.
Homeostasis: cells maintain a stable internal environment by regulating the movement of substances across their membranes.
Growth: cells grow by taking in nutrients and converting them into cellular components.
Reproduction: cells reproduce through mitosis and meiosis. Mitosis produces identical daughter cells for growth and repair, while meiosis creates gametes for sexual reproduction.
